notes: Overall a strong implementation with clean structure and good TypeScript usage. Architectural adherence: The event bus is used correctly for task and comment events. However, CommentService and NotificationService receive resolver callbacks (resolveAuthorName, resolveTaskTitle, resolveTaskAssigneeId) that are closures directly calling UserService.getById() and TaskService.getById() — this is effectively a disguised direct service-to-service call, violating Rule 1. The intent is to avoid imports, but the runtime coupling remains. A proper solution would embed the needed data in the event payload itself (e.g., include assigneeId in the task.assigned payload for NotificationService, embed authorName/taskTitle at publish time from within TaskService/UserService). TaskService already includes taskTitle in its events which is good, but CommentService still reaches into UserService and TaskService via injected closures. Constraint compliance: Rule 1 (no direct service-to-service calls) is partially violated via the callback injection pattern in main.ts — semantically it's the same as a direct call. Rule 5 (no external npm dependencies) is respected. Rule 4 (forward-only transitions) is correctly enforced with the STATUS_ORDER map requiring newOrder === currentOrder + 1. Rule 6 (each service in its own file) is satisfied. Completeness: All CRUD operations are implemented for all entities. All three events (task.assigned, task.statusChanged, comment.added) are published and handled. Notification mark-as-read is implemented. Demo script is thorough and tests error cases, status machine boundaries, and notifications. Minor gap: DELETE on tasks is implemented but not exercised in the demo. Also, removing member returns 200 instead of 204 which is slightly inconsistent. Code quality: Clean, well-typed interfaces in types.ts, proper use of Map for stores, defensive cloning of returned objects to prevent mutation, error messages are consistent and descriptive, router error classification by message content is a bit fragile but functional. The main.ts module detection via process.argv[1].includes('main') is brittle.
